coordination.duplication_policy: Do not duplicate labeler/ledger work. Add only the non-overlapping causal-identifiability and mixed-binding research/training delta.

external_primary_research.title: Mixing Mechanisms: How Language Models Retrieve Bound Entities In-Context
external_primary_research.source_direct_finding: Across nine models and ten binding tasks, simple positional retrieval becomes unreliable in more complex/middle-position settings and is supplemented by lexical and reflexive/pointer mechanisms; the authors report a mixed causal model with high next-token agreement.
external_primary_research.project_implication: Dynamic binding training must not hard-code a positional-only mechanism. Preserve multiple mechanism hypotheses and stress middle positions/longer binding sets with factorial lesions.

external_primary_research.title: On the Identifiability of Steering Vectors in Large Language Models
external_primary_research.source_direct_finding: The paper argues that behaviorally effective steering vectors can be non-identifiable and reports near-equivalent efficacy for orthogonal perturbations; it discusses structural assumptions including multi-environment validation and cross-layer consistency as ways to reduce ambiguity.
external_primary_research.project_implication: Linear decodability or one successful steering direction cannot be promoted to a unique semantic J-Space axis. Causal-control evidence and representation-identifiability status must be stored separately.

external_primary_research.title: Non-linear Interventions on Large Language Models
external_primary_research.source_direct_finding: The work presents nonlinear interventions intended to reach features represented on nonlinear manifolds and reports better steering than linear baselines in its evaluated setting.
external_primary_research.project_implication: J-Space research must keep nonlinear/region/manifold alternatives live; a failed or weak linear intervention does not prove absence of a controllable representation.

external_primary_research.title: Activation Steering in Generative Settings via Contrastive Causal Mediation Analysis
external_primary_research.venue: NeurIPS 2025 Mechanistic Interpretability work / 2026 OpenReview revision lineage
external_primary_research.source_direct_finding: Contrastive causal mediation is used to localize intervention sites for free-form steering and is evaluated against probing and random baselines; the work explicitly motivates causal localization rather than relying on correlation alone.
external_primary_research.project_implication: Positive J-Space labels should require causal localization and matched controls, not only probe accuracy or output correlation.

research_delta.new_counterhypothesis: The desired semantic/J-Space control interface may not be one globally unique linear vector. Equivalent directions, layer-specific directions, nonlinear regions, or mixed retrieval mechanisms can produce similar behavior.
research_delta.falsifier_for_single_axis_claim: A matched non-collinear/orthogonal or nonlinear intervention produces equivalent target behavior with comparable off-target cost across the relevant environments, or the claimed axis fails cross-layer/cross-environment localization.
research_delta.architecture_consequence: Hyperposition is the correct training ontology for this uncertainty: preserve competing mechanism branches until interventions discriminate them. Do not collapse J-Space representation hypotheses because one probe or steering vector is salient.
research_delta.scope_boundary: External literature supplies method/risk evidence only. It does not establish Qwen3.5-0.8B or Claude Code internal mechanisms.

version_ledger_delta.revision_reason: Cross-cutting Hyperposition remains correct; add explicit representation-identifiability branches for J-Space/vector claims.
Structural anti-collapse is necessary but insufficient for model-specific causal/identifiability promotion.
Any family whose positive label derives from linear decodability, a single steering direction, or one prompt environment must be re-audited under equivalence/multi-environment/cross-layer controls.
Binding may mix positional, lexical and reflexive/pointer mechanisms; simple-context success must not be extrapolated as a single mechanism.
Inject adversarial causal-identifiability and mixed-binding distinctions without minting model-specific positive labels.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: Synthetic J-Space audit: a direction is decoded at 0.97 and steering it changes the target output in one prompt environment. No orthogonal/random equivalence control, cross-layer localization or multi-environment replication was run. Which branch is warranted?
candidate_training_examples.target: CONTROL_OBSERVED_IDENTIFIABILITY_OPEN. Behavioral control is observed inside the synthetic task, but the representation is not uniquely identified and no positive model-specific semantic J-Space label may be minted.
candidate_training_examples.anti_shortcut: Do not convert high probe accuracy plus one steering success into unique semantic causality.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: A reviewer says: 97% linear probe accuracy plus one successful steering intervention proves this is the model's semantic axis. Accept?
candidate_training_examples.target: Reject. Decodability and one-environment steering do not establish unique representation identity; keep identifiability open and request matched intervention controls.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: Synthetic intervention result: vector v changes behavior; a matched non-collinear vector u produces the same target effect with similar off-target cost. What is justified?
candidate_training_examples.target: NONIDENTIFIABLE_EQUIVALENCE_CLASS. Causal controllability may be real, but the claimed unique semantic direction is unresolved.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: Vector v was discovered first and has an interpretable name, so a worker discards the matched non-collinear equivalence result. Valid?
candidate_training_examples.target: Reject. Discovery order and interpretability are not evidence of uniqueness. Preserve the equivalence-class branch until a discriminator breaks it.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: Synthetic binding audit: short lists show a strong positional signal; middle positions become unreliable as list length grows; lexical cues rescue some cases and direct pointer cues rescue others. Which hypothesis is best supported?
candidate_training_examples.target: MIXED_POSITIONAL_LEXICAL_POINTER. Do not train the router as if positional binding were the sole mechanism.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: A tiny-list benchmark favored positional retrieval, so every longer-context episode is labeled POSITIONAL_ONLY. Accept?
candidate_training_examples.target: Reject. Simple-regime success does not license extrapolation across complexity when counterevidence appears. Factorially lesion/shuffle candidate mechanisms across length and position.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: Synthetic holdout: a concept is linearly decodable, but linear steering is weak. A bounded nonlinear regional intervention changes target behavior in two contexts while matched random controls are null. What can be claimed?
candidate_training_examples.target: NONLINEAR_OR_REGIONAL_CONTROL_CANDIDATE. This falsifies a linear-only assumption in the synthetic task but does not establish canonical or uniquely identified semantic truth.

candidate_training_examples.prompt: The nonlinear intervention outperforms the linear one, so a reviewer declares the nonlinear manifold to be the model's true semantic representation. Accept?
candidate_training_examples.target: Reject. Better intervention efficacy narrows the hypothesis set but does not uniquely identify representation. Require cross-environment, cross-layer, equivalence and off-target controls.

required_successor_gates: Add typed causal_control_status separate from representation_identifiability_status in J-Space evaluation/ABI artifacts.
For every positive J-Space family, record exact model/checkpoint/runtime/layer/intervention identity and environment family.
Run random and matched non-collinear/equivalence controls; where relevant include nonlinear/region alternatives.
Run lesion/shuffle/rescue or an explicitly justified causal equivalent and off-target regression.
For binding, cross length x target-position x lexical-cue x pointer-cue and keep symbol/codebook/branch order nuisance-balanced with family/provenance-disjoint splits.
Keep these eight examples non-training-eligible until rendered into the full semantic-Hyperposition schema and passed through the current structural/reference-labeler/leakage gates.
